items.title: Critical Care Evidence Updates – August 2026
items.summary: A month of critical care literature in one pass, including a new guideline on cardiac ultrasound in cardiovascular emergency and critical care.
items.note: The cardiac ultrasound entry is what earns this a slot over the usual monthly roundup — it maps onto CCPU cardiac material rather than sitting adjacent to it. The same list carries European diagnostic criteria for cardiogenic shock and the RRT-in-AKI guidelines, both of which decide disposition arguments. This is the critical-care sibling of the Emergency Evidence Updates already in the feed, not a repeat of it.

items.title: Pulmonary haemorrhage in a toddler: when pneumonia isn't pneumonia
items.summary: A toddler who looks like a straightforward chest infection until the diagnosis turns out to be bleeding, not consolidation.
items.note: Paediatric respiratory distress is the presentation where anchoring does the most damage, because the common answer is right often enough to feel safe. DFTB writes these as the case unfolded rather than as a finished review, so the moment the story stops fitting pneumonia is visible rather than asserted. Posted this week and short enough to read between patients.

items.title: ToxCard: Arsenic Toxicity
items.summary: A man arrives with vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain after handling an old pesticide, and the tox differential is the whole case.
items.note: Acute arsenic is the diagnosis nobody makes on the first pass because it arrives dressed as gastro, and the exposure history is the only thing that separates them. The ToxCard format gives the presentation, the chelation decision and the disposition in one screen, which is the right depth for something you will see once and need to get right. It follows the ECG Pointers piece already in the feed from the same shop.

items.title: Royal Children's Hospital beds to go unused, no funding to staff them
items.summary: Twenty new emergency beds at the RCH are finished and cannot open, because the $50m expansion came without money to staff them.
items.note: This is the Victorian ED capacity story in its clearest form: the constraint was never the physical bed. Senior medical staff put their frustration in writing, and one option on the table is moving staff out of other parts of the hospital — redistribution, not new capacity. How the RCH is resourced sets the tone for every other Victorian ED expansion in the pipeline.

items.title: Queensland health service expands AI scribe rollout
items.summary: Metro South is putting an ambient AI scribe across five hospitals — Australia's largest deployment — after a trial claimed 59 minutes saved per doctor per day.
items.note: This is the AI story that actually reaches a registrar's shift, as distinct from benchmark announcements. The 59-minute figure comes from the health service's own trial, so read it as a number with an owner; the RACGP and AHPRA positions still require a human to review every generated note before it lands in the record. Whatever Metro South learns over the next year is the template Victorian services get handed.

items.title: Situation Report No. 9 – Earthquake and Tsunami in Flores
items.summary: The coordination picture from Flores nine reports in, once international attention has moved on and the response is still running.
items.note: Flores is close enough that Australian medical assistance teams are part of the conversation, and far enough down the news cycle that the sitreps are the only continuous record left. These documents are where the shape of a response is legible — cluster gaps, health and shelter coverage, what is still unmet in week three. The feed already follows Nepal and Sudan through the same lens.

items.title: Where to Start With the Essential Jazz and Soul of Mainstream Records
items.summary: A way into Bob Shad's early-'70s Mainstream catalogue, where established jazz singers were pushed into funk and it worked.
items.note: This is the same shape as the Colemine label guide already in the feed, pointed at the label that sits historically upstream of the Daptone and Big Crown shelf. The pull for this collection is specific: Sarah Vaughan singing Marvin Gaye's 'Inner City Blues' with Joe Pass and Earl Palmer behind her, which is Let's Get It On territory approached from the jazz side. Wewantsounds has kept most of it in print, so it is a buyable list rather than a discography.

items.title: How to Save Money on Film
items.summary: A costed look at what a roll actually comes to in 2026 and where the savings are real rather than false economy.
items.note: Average film has settled near US$15 a roll and Australian shelf pricing sits above that before you have paid a lab — which quietly changes how you shoot, not just what you spend. Analog.Cafe does the arithmetic per frame instead of per roll, which is the point at which Kentmere and Gold stop reading as a compromise. Posted today, alongside the ORWO contrast piece already in the feed.

items.title: Giving my Nikon 35Ti some exercise
items.summary: Grey takes the 35Ti out on expired Neopan 400 and writes about the using of it rather than the owning of it.
items.note: The 35Ti is the compact that gets talked about for its analogue dials and almost never for what the pictures look like; Grey shoots it on stock that is past date and reports both honestly. He posts near-daily and rarely reviews anything he has not carried for a while, which is why this feed keeps coming back to him over the gear sites. Follows his Pentax ME piece already in the archive.

items.title: Introducing: The Autumn Overshirt
items.summary: A grey herringbone wool-cashmere overshirt built to work as outerwear now and as a mid-layer once it gets properly cold.
items.note: The overshirt does most of the work in a Melbourne shoulder season, and Crompton is unusually specific about cloth weight and why this one sits where it does between jacket and knit. Read it for the cloth reasoning rather than the shop listing — the argument transfers straight to what to look for in a vintage Woolrich or Pendleton version. PS stock moves fast, which is the only genuinely timely part.

items.title: The Witcher 4 will release in a box, even if it can't contain a disc
items.summary: CD Projekt commits to a physical Witcher 4 edition while conceding Sony may not be pressing PlayStation discs by 2028.
items.note: Nowakowski is unusually blunt that PlayStation discs are made in Sony's own plants and CDPR has no say if those stop in January 2028, so the box may hold a download code and collectibles instead. That is the end of physical PS releases being confirmed sideways, through a game still two years out. Rockstar is already doing the same with the GTA VI physical edition in November — this follows the Witcher 4 release-window piece already in the feed.

items.title: Champagne Video Is a New Fitzroy North Cinema and Bar
items.summary: A thirty-seat screening room, a bar and a working video rental counter, in the old Wildflower Picture House.
items.note: Jack White, who runs Henkel Street Cinema in Brunswick, has taken the Wildflower site and put DVDs and VHS back on the walls to rent Blockbuster-style. It is the same northside single-screen impulse as the Thornbury Picture House team's new Brunswick cinema already in the feed, except this one leans on the bar and the pre-streaming back catalogue. Named for the rental store in Seinfeld, which tells you the register it is pitched at.
